title: Postcard and Garden
premise: Xanthe Voss has spent ten years in the small coastal town of Marrow Bay hiding behind her bookshop and her daughter, avoiding the family that once destroyed her mother's reputation. When her sister's engagement party forces her to attend, she recruits Theo Marchetti, a visiting restorer working on the town hall murals, to pose as her boyfriend. The fake date turns real, but Xanthe's rehearsed confession—that her powerful uncle falsified the evidence that ruined her mother—collides with Theo's discovery that his own restoration contract is funded by the same man. As the truth surfaces publicly, Xanthe must choose between safety and justice, ultimately testifying at a hearing that strips her uncle of influence, while choosing love not as escape but as an equal partnership.
about_author: Ines Kavanagh is a former small-town librarian who writes romances about people who rebuild their lives one stubborn act at a time. She lives by the sea with two cats and an unreasonable collection of secondhand postcards.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Opening on a rainy Tuesday in the bookshop, we learn she has carried a sealed letter for ten years—the truth about her uncle Aldous—and rehearses saying it aloud to no one. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Invitation, Embossed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. An invitation to her sister Priya's engagement party arrives; her mother begs her to come, and her aunt warns Aldous will be there. Xanthe refuses, then finds a postcard from her late grandmother urging courage. Beat: guilt tightening like a knot.

chapters.title: The Man on the Ladder
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo Marchetti, a mural restorer hired for the town hall, wanders into the shop seeking a book on pigments. Their banter sparks something neither expects. Beat: unexpected warmth cracking Xanthe's armor.

chapters.title: A Reasonable Lie
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Cornered by her aunt into attending the reunion 'with someone,' Xanthe impulsively asks Theo to be her fake date. He agrees, curious about why she flinches at her own family name. Beat: reckless hope.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Disaster
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over coffee, they invent a meet-cute story; Theo notices Xanthe recites facts about herself like testimony rather than memory. Beat: intimacy beginning under the cover of fiction.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The reunion at the Voss estate: Aldous charming and watchful, Priya radiant, Xanthe performing happiness with Theo's hand steady in hers. Beat: terror and exhilaration braided together.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Between courses, Theo defends Xanthe against a snide cousin, and their staged chemistry stops being staged. On the terrace, they almost kiss before Aldous interrupts. Beat: the lie turning true.

chapters.title: What the Murals Remember
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Restoring the town hall frescoes, Theo uncovers a painted-over panel dated the year Xanthe's mother was disgraced—and finds Aldous's name in the donor ledger. Beat: suspicion kindling.

chapters.title: Postcards from Before
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Sorting her grandmother's things, Xanthe rereads old postcards hinting her mother was framed over missing trust funds. Her daughter Ivy asks why Grandma never visits. Beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Second Date, First Truths
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A real date, no pretense; Xanthe tells Theo about raising Ivy alone but stops short of the letter. Theo, holding back what he found, feels the asymmetry. Beat: closeness shadowed by secrets.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts his employer's firm about the mural funding trail and discovers Aldous Voss bankrolled the restoration to launder his civic image. Threatened with contract termination, he photographs everything. Beat: loyalty tested by conscience.

chapters.title: Priya's Doubt
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya finds one of grandmother's postcards in Xanthe's coat and begins questioning the family story she inherited. She almost asks Aldous directly, then falters. Beat: the first crack inside the fortress.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Aldous visits the bookshop, offering money for Ivy's education if Xanthe 'lets the past stay buried.' She recognizes the threat beneath the generosity. Beat: fear transmuting into anger.

chapters.title: Broken Glass, Broken Trust
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Xanthe learns Theo knew about the ledger and said nothing; Theo learns she's been sitting on a decade-old letter. They fight, each accusing the other of the same silence. Beat: heartbreak mirroring the theme.

chapters.title: Ivy's Question
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV (child's voice). Ivy, doing a school project on family history, asks why there are no photos of Grandmother's brother. Her innocent research surfaces a newspaper clipping. Beat: truth arriving through the smallest witness.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed for a Decade
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At her mother's kitchen table, Xanthe finally reads the letter aloud to her mother—who reveals she always suspected but was too afraid. Together they decide to speak. Beat: catharsis and shared courage.

chapters.title: Allies at Midnight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo returns with copies of the ledger; he and Xanthe reconcile, not with a grand gesture but with honesty. Priya joins them, bringing the estate's private correspondence. Beat: fragile alliance formed.

chapters.title: The Engagement Party Reckoning
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At Priya's second celebration, Xanthe stands before the assembled family and says the sentence: Aldous fabricated the evidence. Chaos erupts; Aldous denies, threatens, and overreaches publicly. Beat: climax—truth spoken at last.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Aldous's lawyers circle; Theo's photographs and the mural ledger reach a journalist and the probate investigator. Xanthe braces for retaliation, guarding Ivy. Beat: tension at its peak, cost made real.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the formal hearing, Xanthe testifies with her mother beside her; Priya corroborates. Aldous's empire of respectability collapses under documented fraud. Beat: justice achieved outside comfort, inside law.

chapters.title: Garden After Frost
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Weeks later, Xanthe plants her grandmother's garden with Ivy while the town digests the scandal. Theo asks to stay—not as an escape from his old life but a choice of this one. Beat: tender renewal.

chapters.title: Postcard, Answered
chapters.summary: Alternating POV closing on Xanthe. Xanthe mails a reply to her grandmother's last postcard, addressed to memory: 'I said it.' In the bookshop doorway, Theo and Ivy wait, and she walks toward them. Beat: peace earned, identity claimed.
